full_judgment:
2. The facts relevant for disposal of the present petition are that the respondent No. 2 Social Investment Bank filed a suit before the Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka for realization of outstanding amount and obtained an ex parte decree of Tk. 6,19,770/-. Against that the petitioner filed writ petition No. 1525 of 2001 and the same was discharged and the order of stay was vacated. Thereafter, the respondent bank filed execution case being Artha Jari Case No. 525 of 2008 and in the proceeding of the said execution case, the petitioner was givens a chance to pay off the loan money within one year as per section 49 (I) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain (herein after referred as the AM) Subsequently, the executions case ended in issuance of certificate in favour of the bank under section 33(5) of the Ain. At this stage the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 6120 of 2011 before the High court Division for taking advantage of section 49 (1) of the Ain and obtained Rule. 

 4. Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that since the delivery of possession of mortgaged property was not handed over to the decree holder bank, and the Bank has not yet submitted title documents under section 33 (7) (Kha) as per order of the Artha Rin Adalat dated 05.04.2011, as such the Artha Jari Case is still pending, and not yet disposed of. The Artha Rin Adalat wrongly observed that since the Artha Jari Case is disposed of in full satisfaction there is no scope to deposit money under section 49 (1) of the Ain without considering the scope of section 49 (I) of the AM. He further submitted that as per order dated 18.05.2011 the petitioner asked to deposit the loan money, accordingly he deposited TK. 50,000/- this aspect of the matter was not considered by the Artha Rin Adalat or the Hon'ble High Court Division. Titus the impugned judgment passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 5. Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. He submitted that after the issuance of certificate under section 33 (7) of the Ain in respect of the mortgaged property, the execution case was disposed of in full satisfaction of the decree. The bank armed with the certificate, on 25.04.2011 applied for issuance of warrant for delivery of possession. He submitted that at that time the writ petitioner did not have any right to apply to cancel the certificate issued under section 33 (7) and for the privilege of payment of the decretal amount by installments under section 49 (1) of the Ain.
